sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests how courts define the start and end of a workday. The dispute centers on whether time spent walking to gear stations and waiting for equipment counts as compensable work.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The employer wants the Court to rule that walking and waiting time are not principal activities and thus unpaid.
The workers want the Court to rule that walking and waiting time are integral to the job and must be paid.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The employer argues that the Portal Act excludes time spent before or after principal activities, which they define as the core production tasks.
The workers argue that previous precedent defines principal activities to include all integral and indispensable tasks, such as changing into required gear.
